summary: Confirmed DONE. All 32 non-test getShellSnapshot callers from f1be4abc7 were checked one by one. Each now uses a narrow read (listProjectShells, getWorkspacePlacement, getProjectWorkspaceRows, getProjectShellById, getSnapshotSequence, listPendingGoalSyncThreads) or a scoped shell read. Five justified whole-shell callers remain, plus 4 test-double fallbacks. The boot path in ProviderCommandReactor.start now runs one filtered SQL read over projection_threads plus projection_state. buildShell is pure SQL: it decodes persisted repository identities and never probes git, so the repositoryIdentity:false variant is moot. A ratchet test enforces exact allowlist counts. The project has one production implementation of the shape (the Layer), and it provides all four optional narrow methods, so the whole-shell fallbacks cannot trigger in production. Only small, low-value residuals remain.

evidence.note: At boot, reactors.start calls readPendingGoalSyncThreads. The filtering for deferUntilTurn and pending state matches the old shell loop at f1be4abc7:3151.
listPendingGoalSyncThreadRows: a filtered SELECT guarded by json_valid. It is read in one transaction with projection_state (:3277-3300). The test is at ProjectionSnapshotQuery.shell.test.ts:225.
The comment confirms buildShell is pure SQL and uses decodePersistedRepositoryIdentity. No RepositoryIdentityResolver remains in this file. The auditor cited :3060; the comment is actually at :3006.
getShellSnapshot is coalesced through coalesceConcurrentRuns (:673), which never serves a result older than the call. Inside a transaction it builds directly.

This is the only production object satisfying ProjectionSnapshotQueryShape. It includes listProjectShells, getWorkspacePlacement, listPendingGoalSyncThreads and getScopedShellSnapshot, so the Services fallbacks (:491-516) are reachable only from test doubles.

The allowlist: orchestrationRpc 1, threadReadCacheShellMirror 1, Services 4, WorkspaceLifecycle 1, StorageService 1, Mcp/threadReads 1. git grep of non-test sources matches exactly. threadFork.fixtures.ts is excluded as a fixture.
buildRestoreNeighbours reads the placement (5 columns per thread), then does a scoped read of only the overlapping threads (:899).

The 4 old calls became getProjectWorkspaceRows (:260), getWorktreeShellById or placement (:275), and readProjectShells in reconcileAllWorktrees (:919). The init-repo attach loop uses loadProjectWorkspaceRows (:1110).

The old shell build under the lifecycle lock (f1be4abc7:731) is now getSnapshotSequence. Other paths use readProjectShells (:1056) and readWorkspacePlacement (:1122). Only inventory() (:120) still builds a whole shell, because it checks session status, pending approvals and goal sync per thread.
This is the remaining per-tool-call whole shell: an unscoped list_threads page, used by Mcp/tools.ts:2103 and ExternalMcp/tools.ts:599. Project-scoped listings use readScopedShellSnapshot.

The cloud index rebuilds the whole shell at most every 60 s, on unmodeled events, or after a failure. Otherwise it patches rows from domain events. It is gated by RYCO_HUB_THREAD_CACHE_ENABLED (default false).
Only the user-triggered lifecycle.suggestions() RPC ('all' scope) builds a whole shell. Other scopes use placement plus a project-scoped read (:435, :444).

fixDefects: No functional defects found. Minor residuals, none of which is a bug: (1) Mcp/threadReads.ts:271: an unscoped list_threads still builds the whole shell on every page call, so paging through 4.5k threads at 50 per page costs about 90 full builds (about 100 ms each, coalesced only when concurrent). (2) StorageService.inventory (:120) runs twice per remove() (:710, :787), sequentially and so without coalescing. An hourly automatic-retention pass that removes up to 20 entries performs up to 41 whole-shell builds. Each inventory also does up to 1.5 s of realpath work, which costs more than the shell. This is background and opt-in, and the repeated inventory is a deliberate re-validation. (3) A scoped buildShell still runs the unscoped listThreadPriorityRows() and filters it in JS (ProjectionSnapshotQuery.ts:3063, :3112). (4) The ratchet regex matches only the literal `.getShellSnapshot(`. It misses getScopedShellSnapshot({}) with an empty scope, which builds an uncoalesced whole shell, and it misses method references passed without parentheses. No current caller does either. (5) In managedWorktreeMigration idle() (:125), the attached-thread SQL does not filter deleted_at. The effect is conservative: deleted threads are dropped by the scoped read but can still count toward the 5000 limit or the binding check.
implementationSketch: This is optional cleanup only; nothing is required. (a) Unscoped MCP listing: add a ProjectionSnapshotQuery.listThreadShellPage({ after: {createdAt,id} | null, includeArchived, limit, projectIds? }) method. It runs a keyset SELECT of thread ids on projection_threads (deleted_at IS NULL, optional archived_at IS NULL, (created_at, thread_id) > cursor, ORDER BY created_at, thread_id, LIMIT n+1), then calls getScopedShellSnapshot({ threadIds }). In threadReads.listThreadsPage, loop by over-fetching until enough rows pass the external visibility predicate or the rows run out. Keep the cursor encoding. Remove the threadReads entry from the ALLOWED_SHELL_SNAPSHOT_CALLERS ratchet. Test: page through 3 pages with mixed archived and hidden threads and assert the same results as the current implementation. (b) Scoped priority rows: pass the scope into listThreadPriorityRows via json_each on ranking.thread_id or a project join. (c) Ratchet hardening: also match `getShellSnapshot\b(?!\s*:)` references, and make getScopedShellSnapshot reject or assert a non-empty scope. (d) StorageService: optionally reuse the scan's inventory for the first per-entry check in runRetention when getSnapshotSequence is unchanged. Keep the post-claim finalContext re-validation.
decisionReason: Server-internal read-path cleanups only. No auth, E2EE, hosted lifecycle or Hub protocol impact.
